input.question: Why, when I'm sick, do I start to feel worse at night? And why do I feel better during/directly after a shower?
input.ground_truth: Depends on the illness and a lot about your physiology. Re: time of day, if you have something like congestion, it's going to vary in its unpleasantness with things like your blood pressure, which go through cycles throughout the day. Your entire body cycles through all sorts of different things that can change how you're feeling. It's possible that when you're out you're just distracted.

At night, your body tries extra hard to fight those germs. It sends out its superhero cells to chase them away. But when the superheroes are fighting, they make you feel even more tired and achy, so you feel worse at night.

Now, when you take a shower, the warm water is like a cozy blanket for your body. It helps your muscles relax and makes you feel a little bit happier. The steam and the warm water can also help your body get rid of some of the icky feeling. That’s why you feel better during or right after a shower!

So, at night, your body is working extra hard to get rid of the germs, and that makes you feel worse. But a warm shower gives you a nice, cozy feeling that helps you feel better for a little while.
